title: St. Louis trumpet players on Sundays
summary: At a St. Louis hotel, Dewey Jackson, Baby James and others played Louis's Hot Five repertoire, which Roy found Southern and not his style.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Then we went from there to St. Louis, and I had a trunk full of clothes. And when I got to St. Louis and the trunk got there, wasn't a stitch in that trunk. Nothing. We stayed around there at that hotel, the Grand Central or Grand Something... And them trumpet players used to come in every Sunday on me -- Dewey Jackson, Baby James, and some big cat, I never did know his name, that looked like Louis Armstrong, a big fat cat... And they all played "Butter And Egg Man"...all of those things that Louis used to play during that time, you know.
Yeah. You know, that still to me was still
that Southern trumpet playing! The only one who was a little different was Dewey Jackson. Then there was Zutty's brother, or brother-in-law...

Yeah. I caught him at a party, you know. I never could figure out where he was... Well, maybe he might have been something, I don't know. He was just... The only one that I got to really like was Baby James. This cat had a nice sound and he played those things of Louis nice, you know. I don't know whatever happened to him.
What was it you didn't like about the others?

Well, the reason that I didn't like them was just... They were just Southern trumpet players. That wasn't the way i wanted to play, you know. Because they were doing, like [CLARION SOUND]...you know, like do. I can do it now, but I wasn't then, you know. Because I was on the kick of the saxophone; I was more leaning towards the saxophone than I was for a trumpet. So naturally, I didn't hear nothin' but clarinets, and those saxophone players really knocked me out, you know.

You see, it was a little different than the New York playing, you know.
